name: Monarch Butterfly
habitat: Meadows, fields, and gardens across North America
funFact: Monarchs migrate up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico each fall.
description: The monarch butterfly is one of the most recognizable butterflies in North America, known for its striking orange and black wing pattern. It is famous for its incredible long-distance migration across thousands of miles.

name: Luna Moth
habitat: Deciduous hardwood forests of North America
funFact: Luna moths do not have mouths and cannot eat as adults, living only on stored energy.
description: The luna moth is a large, pale green moth with long tail-like hindwings. It is nocturnal and attracted to light, and adults do not feed, dedicating their brief adult lives entirely to reproduction.

name: Atlas Moth
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests of Southeast Asia
funFact: The atlas moth is one of the largest insects in the world by wing area.
description: The atlas moth is the largest moth species, with a wingspan that can exceed 12 inches. Its wings have snake-head-shaped tips that deter predators, and like other giant moths, adults do not feed.

name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
funFact: Female swallowtails can mimic the toxic pipevine swallowtail to avoid predators.
description: The eastern tiger swallowtail is a large, bright yellow butterfly with distinctive black tiger stripes. It is one of the most common and recognizable butterflies in eastern North America.

name: Hawk Moth
habitat: Gardens, woodlands, and tropical forests worldwide
funFact: Hawk moths are among the fastest flying insects, capable of hovering like hummingbirds.
description: Hawk moths, also known as sphinx moths, are powerful fliers with streamlined bodies. Many species have extremely long proboscises for feeding on deep-throated flowers while hovering.

name: Painted Lady Butterfly
habitat: Meadows, gardens, and open fields worldwide
funFact: Painted ladies migrate across the Sahara Desert and the Mediterranean Sea.
description: The painted lady is one of the most widespread butterflies on Earth, found on every continent except Antarctica. It is a strong migrant and a common visitor to gardens.

name: Blue Morpho Butterfly
habitat: Tropical rainforests of Central and South America
funFact: The morpho's blue color is not pigment but structural coloration from microscopic scales.
description: The blue morpho is a brilliantly iridescent blue butterfly found in tropical rainforests. Its metallic blue wings are visible from great distances and are produced by light diffraction rather than pigment.

name: Glasswing Butterfly
funFact: The glasswing butterfly has nearly transparent wings due to nanopillar structures.
description: The glasswing butterfly has remarkably transparent wings with only a thin dark border. The transparency is caused by tiny nanopillar structures on the wings that prevent light reflection.

name: Cecropia Moth
habitat: Deciduous forests of eastern North America
funFact: The cecropia moth is the largest native moth in North America.
description: The cecropia moth is North America's largest moth with wingspans reaching 7 inches. It has striking red, orange, and white markings and, like other giant moths, adults do not feed.

name: Io Moth
habitat: Deciduous forests and shrublands of eastern North America
funFact: Each wing of the io moth has a large, striking eyespot that deters predators.
description: The io moth is a beautiful silk moth with large eyespots on each wing. Males are yellow while females are reddish-brown, and both sexes flash their eyespots when threatened.

name: Polyphemus Moth
habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests of North America
funFact: The polyphemus moth is named after the one-eyed Greek giant Polyphemus.
description: The polyphemus moth is a large, tan-colored silk moth with distinctive eyespots on its hindwings. It is named after the Cyclops of Greek mythology due to the large eyespots.

name: Viceroy Butterfly
funFact: Viceroys mimic the toxic monarch butterfly for protection from predators.
description: The viceroy butterfly closely resembles the monarch and was long thought to be a mimic. It is now known to be somewhat distasteful to predators, making it a Müllerian mimic.

name: Red Admiral Butterfly
funFact: Red admirals are territorial and will chase other butterflies from their favorite basking spots.
description: The red admiral is a striking black butterfly with bold red-orange bands and white spots. It is a strong flier found worldwide and often visits rotting fruit and tree sap.

name: Great Spangled Fritillary
funFact: Fritillary caterpillars feed exclusively on violets, which is how the group got its name.
description: The great spangled fritillary is a large, orange butterfly with distinctive silver-spotted underwings. Its larvae feed on various violet species while adults nectar on milkweed and coneflowers.

name: Clouded Yellow
habitat: Meadows, pastures, and farmland across Europe and Asia
funFact: Clouded yellows are strong migrants that can travel hundreds of miles.
description: The clouded yellow is a bright golden butterfly common across Europe and parts of Asia. It is a strong migratory species that sometimes appears in large numbers in areas outside its normal range.

name: Comma Butterfly
funFact: The comma butterfly is named for the small white comma-shaped mark on its underwings.
description: The comma butterfly has uniquely ragged wing edges that help camouflage it as a dead leaf. It has a distinctive white comma-shaped mark on its dark brown underwings.

name: Mourning Cloak Butterfly
funFact: The mourning cloak is one of the longest-lived butterflies and overwinters as an adult.
description: The mourning cloak is one of the longest-lived butterflies, surviving up to 11 months. It overwinters as an adult and is often the first butterfly seen in spring, with dark wings bordered in yellow.

name: Zebra Longwing Butterfly
funFact: Zebra longwings are the state butterfly of Florida and can live on pollen alone.
description: The zebra longwing is a distinctive butterfly with black wings marked by pale yellow stripes. It is unique among butterflies in that adults can digest pollen, extending their lifespan significantly.
region: Southern United States, Central America, and South America

name: Snowflake Butterfly
habitat: Tropical forests of Central and South America
funFact: The snowflake butterfly has mostly white wings with delicate black tips.
description: The snowflake butterfly is a delicate white butterfly found in tropical forests. Its mostly white wings with small dark tips give it a graceful appearance as it glides through forest understory.

name: Resurrection Butterfly
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests of East Asia
funFact: The resurrection butterfly is considered a symbol of rebirth in Japanese culture.
description: The resurrection butterfly, known as Kuroneko Yamane in Japan, is a medium-sized butterfly with distinctive markings. It has deep cultural significance in Japan as a symbol of love and resurrection.

name: Small White Butterfly
habitat: Gardens, farmlands, and disturbed areas worldwide
funFact: The small white is one of the most common butterflies in the world and a notorious garden pest.
description: The small white butterfly is a widespread species often found in gardens and agricultural areas. Its caterpillars are major pests of cabbage and other brassica crops.

name: Atlas Beetle
funFact: Atlas beetles can carry objects 850 times their own body weight.
description: The atlas beetle is a large rhinoceros beetle native to Southeast Asian rainforests. Males have three prominent horns used in combat for mates, and they are among the strongest insects relative to size.

name: Goliath Beetle
habitat: Tropical rainforests and savannas of Africa
funFact: Goliath beetles are among the heaviest insects in the world.
description: The goliath beetle is one of the largest and heaviest insects on Earth, found in African tropical forests. They feed on fruit and tree sap, and their larvae are among the heaviest grubs known.

name: Western Hercules Beetle
funFact: Rhinoceros beetles can lift objects 850 times their own body weight.
description: The western hercules beetle is a large rhinoceros beetle found in the hardwood forests of North America. Males have a distinctive horn used for wrestling other males during mating season.

name: Stag Beetle
funFact: Male stag beetles use their enormous mandibles to wrestle rivals for mates.
description: Stag beetles are named for the large, antler-like mandibles of the males. They spend most of their lives as larvae feeding on decaying wood underground before emerging as impressive adults.

name: Common Eastern Firefly
funFact: Firefly larvae glow too, and some produce light to deter predators.
description: Fireflies are beetles famous for their bioluminescent abdomens used to attract mates. Both adults and larvae produce light through a chemical reaction involving luciferin and luciferase.

name: Scarab Dung Beetle
funFact: Dung beetles navigate using the Milky Way, the first insects found to use stars.
description: Dung beetles roll animal droppings into balls for food or breeding. They are essential decomposers that help recycle nutrients back into the soil and reduce parasite populations in pastures.

name: Seven-Spotted Ladybug
funFact: A single ladybug can eat up to 5,000 aphids in its lifetime.
description: Ladybugs are small, round beetles valued by gardeners for their appetite for aphids and other plant pests. Their bright red coloration with black spots warns predators of their bitter taste.

name: Six-Spotted Tiger Beetle
habitat: Sandy paths, mudflats, and forest edges
funFact: Tiger beetles run so fast they go temporarily blind because their eyes cannot process images quickly enough.
description: Tiger beetles are fast-running predatory beetles with large eyes and powerful jaws. They are voracious hunters of smaller insects and are often found on open, sunlit ground.

name: Asian Longhorned Beetle
funFact: The Asian longhorned beetle can kill healthy hardwood trees by tunneling through their bark.
description: The Asian longhorned beetle is an invasive species that attacks a wide variety of hardwood trees. It has distinctive black and white markings and very long antennae that exceed its body length.
region: East Asia (invasive in North America and Europe)

name: Click Beetle
funFact: Click beetles can launch themselves into the air with a clicking mechanism without using their legs.
description: Click beetles have a unique clicking mechanism on their thorax that allows them to snap and launch into the air when overturned. Their larvae, called wireworms, are important soil dwellers.

name: Bombardier Beetle
funFact: Bombardier beetles spray a boiling chemical spray at 212 degrees Fahrenheit from their abdomen.
description: The bombardier beetle defends itself by ejecting a hot, noxious chemical spray from its abdomen with an audible pop. The spray reaches temperatures near boiling and repels predators effectively.

name: June Bug
funFact: June bugs are clumsy fliers and often bounce off windows and walls.
description: June bugs are chunky, brown beetles that emerge in late spring. They are attracted to lights at night and their larvae, known as white grubs, feed on grass roots and can damage lawns.

name: Whirligig Beetle
funFact: Whirligig beetles have four eyes: two for seeing above water and two for seeing below.
description: Whirligig beetles are aquatic beetles that spin rapidly on the surface of calm water. They have split eyes adapted for both aerial and aquatic vision and are social insects that form groups.

name: Predaceous Diving Beetle
funFact: Diving beetles carry an air bubble under their wing covers to breathe underwater.
description: Predaceous diving beetles are streamlined aquatic predators that hunt tadpoles, small fish, and other insects underwater. They trap air beneath their elytra for extended submerged hunting.

name: Oil Beetle
funFact: Oil beetles secrete oily droplets from their joints that repel predators and can blister human skin.
description: Oil beetles are flightless blister beetles that produce cantharidin, a toxic oily substance, from their joints. Their larvae parasitize solitary bees and develop inside their nests.

name: Bess Beetle
habitat: Decaying logs and stumps in forests
funFact: Bess beetles communicate by rubbing their abdomen to make squeaking sounds.
description: Bess beetles are large, shiny black beetles that live in decaying wood. They exhibit parental care, with adults feeding and caring for their larvae, which is unusual for beetles.

name: Mountain Pine Beetle
funFact: Mountain pine beetle outbreaks can kill millions of acres of forest in a single year.
description: Mountain pine beetles are tiny bark beetles that bore into pine trees and introduce blue-stain fungi. Massive outbreaks have devastated millions of acres of forest in western North America.

name: Sacred Scarab Beetle
habitat: Grasslands and pastures of Africa and Mediterranean
funFact: Ancient Egyptians revered the scarab as a symbol of the sun god Khepri.
description: The sacred scarab beetle rolls dung into balls and was revered in ancient Egyptian culture as a symbol of rebirth and the sun's daily journey across the sky.

name: American Carrion Beetle
habitat: Forests and areas with decaying matter
funFact: Carrion beetles can locate a dead animal from over a mile away using chemical sensors.
description: The American carrion beetle is a large, flat beetle that feeds on dead animals and snails. It plays an important ecological role in recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

name: Patrol Bess Beetle
funFact: Patrol bess beetles produce sounds by rubbing ridges on their abdomen when disturbed.
description: The patrol bess beetle is a large, glossy black beetle found in tropical rainforests. Like other passalid beetles, both parents work together to feed and care for their larvae.

name: Eyed Click Beetle
funFact: The eyed click beetle has two large eyespots on its thorax that startle predators.
description: The eyed click beetle is a large click beetle with distinctive eyespots on its pronotum. When threatened, it clicks and flips into the air to right itself or escape danger.

name: Rose Chafer
funFact: Rose chafers can fly with their elytra closed, using only their hind wings.
description: The rose chafer is a metallic green beetle that feeds on flowers, especially roses and fruit blossoms. Despite being considered a pest, its larvae help decompose organic matter in soil.

name: Japanese Beetle
funFact: Japanese beetles release aggregation pheromones that attract more beetles to feed.
description: The Japanese beetle is a highly invasive pest that skeletonizes leaves and damages turf with its white grub larvae. It is native to Japan and has become a devastating pest in North America.
region: East Asia (invasive in North America and Europe)

name: Colorado Potato Beetle
habitat: Potato fields and solanaceous crop areas
funFact: The Colorado potato beetle is one of the most insecticide-resistant pests in the world.
description: The Colorado potato beetle is a major agricultural pest that feeds on potatoes, tomatoes, and eggplants. It has developed resistance to over 50 different insecticides.

name: Scarlet Lily Beetle
funFact: Lily beetles are bright red, making them easy to spot on green leaves.
description: The scarlet lily beetle is a bright red pest of lily plants. Both adults and larvae feed on leaves, stems, and flowers, and the larvae cover themselves in their own excrement for protection.

name: Elm Leaf Beetle
habitat: Near elm trees in urban and suburban areas
funFact: Elm leaf beetles can enter homes through small cracks and hibernate indoors during winter.
description: The elm leaf beetle skeletonizes elm tree leaves and is a significant urban pest. Adults often overwinter inside buildings, emerging in spring to feed on newly emerged elm leaves.

name: Red Imported Fire Ant
funFact: Fire ant colonies can form living rafts that float on water for weeks during floods.
description: Red imported fire ants are invasive ants native to South America that deliver painful stings causing burning welts. They build large mound nests and can survive flooding by forming floating colonies.

name: Leafcutter Ant
habitat: Tropical forests of Central and South America
funFact: Leafcutter ants are the largest consumers of vegetation in the Neotropics.
description: Leafcutter ants cut and carry pieces of leaves back to their nests to feed a special fungus that they cultivate. They are sophisticated farmers with complex division of labor among castes.

name: Bullet Ant
habitat: Lowland rainforests of Central and South America
funFact: The bullet ant's sting is rated as the most painful insect sting in the world.
description: The bullet ant gets its name from the intense pain of its sting, which has been compared to being shot. Indigenous tribes use bullet ant stings in coming-of-age rituals.

name: Army Ant
habitat: Tropical forests of Africa and the Americas
funFact: Army ant colonies of millions move in massive raiding columns that devour everything in their path.
description: Army ants are nomadic predators that form massive raiding swarms. They do not build permanent nests but instead form living bivouacs made of their own bodies while the colony rests.

name: Trap-Jaw Ant
habitat: Tropical forests of Southeast Asia and the Americas
funFact: Trap-jaw ants can snap their mandibles at speeds exceeding 140 mph.
description: Trap-jaw ants have spring-loaded mandibles that snap shut at incredible speeds to capture prey and can also use the force to launch themselves into the air to escape predators.

name: Weaver Ant
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests of Asia and Australia
funFact: Weaver ants use their own larvae as living glue guns to stitch leaves together.
description: Weaver ants build elaborate nests by weaving living leaves together using silk produced by their larvae. They are aggressive defenders of their territory and tend honeydew-producing insects.

name: Western Honeybee
habitat: Meadows, gardens, and agricultural areas worldwide
funFact: A single honeybee colony can visit over 225,000 flowers to produce one pound of honey.
description: The western honeybee is the world's most important pollinator of agricultural crops. They live in highly organized colonies with complex social structures and produce honey and beeswax.

name: Common Bumblebee
funFact: Bumblebees can fly in colder temperatures than most bees due to their ability to thermoregulate.
description: Bumblebees are robust, fuzzy bees important for pollinating wildflowers and crops. They are capable of buzz pollination, vibrating their flight muscles to release pollen from flowers.

name: Eastern Carpenter Bee
habitat: Forests, gardens, and near wooden structures
funFact: Carpenter bees drill perfectly round holes in wood to create nesting galleries.
description: Carpenter bees are large, solitary bees that bore into untreated wood to create nesting tunnels. Despite their intimidating size, they are gentle and rarely sting, preferring to hover near structures.

name: European Paper Wasp
funFact: Paper wasps build their nests from chewed wood fibers mixed with saliva.
description: Paper wasps are slender wasps with long legs that build open-comb umbrella-shaped nests from wood pulp. They are beneficial predators of caterpillars but will sting if their nest is threatened.

name: Common Yellow Jacket
funFact: Yellow jacket colonies can grow to contain 4,000 or more workers by late summer.
description: Yellow jackets are aggressive wasps known for their bright yellow and black markings. They build enclosed paper nests and are notorious for scavenging at picnics and outdoor events.

name: Bald-Faced Hornet
habitat: Forests and suburban areas of eastern North America
funFact: Bald-faced hornets can spray venom from their stingers up to several feet.
description: Despite its name, the bald-faced hornet is actually a yellowjacket, not a true hornet. It builds large, enclosed paper nests high in trees and is known for its aggressive defense of its colony.

name: European Hornet
funFact: European hornets are attracted to light and will often fly into homes at night.
description: The European hornet is the largest social wasp in Europe and an invasive species in North America. Queens can reach 1.4 inches in length, and colonies can contain up to 1,000 workers.

name: Tarantula Hawk Wasp
habitat: Deserts and scrublands of the Americas
funFact: The tarantula hawk has one of the most painful insect stings in the world.
description: The tarantula hawk is a large, metallic blue-black wasp that hunts tarantulas to serve as live food for its larvae. Its sting is excruciatingly painful but rarely dangerous to humans.

name: Cuckoo Wasp
habitat: Sandy areas and near host bee nests
funFact: Cuckoo wasps can curl into a ball when threatened, using their armored exoskeleton for protection.
description: Cuckoo wasps are brilliant metallic blue or green parasitoids that lay their eggs in the nests of other bees and wasps. Their larvae consume the host's eggs or larvae and stored food.

name: Giant Ichneumon Wasp
habitat: Forests with dead or dying trees
funFact: The giant ichneumon's ovipositor can be longer than its body and drills through wood to reach beetle larvae.
description: Giant ichneumon wasps are parasitoids that use their extremely long ovipositors to drill into wood and lay eggs inside wood-boring beetle larvae. Despite their fearsome appearance, they cannot sting humans.

name: Asian Giant Hornet
habitat: Forests and mountains of East Asia
funFact: The Asian giant hornet can decapitate an entire honeybee colony in hours.
description: The Asian giant hornet, nicknamed the murder hornet, is the world's largest hornet. Its powerful sting delivers potent venom and it is a devastating predator of honeybee colonies.

name: Sweat Bee
funFact: Some sweat bees have metallic green or blue bodies that shimmer in the sunlight.
description: Sweat bees are small, often metallic-colored bees attracted to human perspiration for its salt content. They are important pollinators and nest in the ground or in hollow stems.

name: Blue Orchard Mason Bee
funFact: Mason bees are 100 times more efficient at pollinating than honeybees.
description: The blue orchard mason bee is a solitary bee that nests in hollow tubes and crevices. It is a far more efficient pollinator than honeybees, visiting far more flowers per hour.

name: Tawny Mining Bee
funFact: Mining bees create small volcano-shaped mounds of soil at their nest entrances.
description: Mining bees are solitary ground-nesting bees that excavate tunnels in soil. They emerge in spring and are important early-season pollinators of fruit trees and wildflowers.

name: Golden Digger Wasp
funFact: Golden digger wasps paralyze grasshoppers and crickets to feed their larvae alive.
description: The golden digger wasp is a large, metallic golden wasp that hunts grasshoppers and crickets. It buries paralyzed prey in underground nests for its developing larvae.

name: Mud Dauber Wasp
funFact: Mud daubers stock their nests with paralyzed spiders for their developing larvae.
description: Mud dauber wasps are solitary wasps that construct tubular mud nests on sheltered surfaces. They hunt and paralyze spiders to stock each cell for their developing young.

name: Horned Mason Bee
habitat: Woodlands and gardens with hollow stems
funFact: Male horned mason bees have small horns on their faces used in mating displays.
description: The horned mason bee is a solitary bee that nests in hollow stems and bee hotels. Males have distinctive facial horns and both sexes are important early-season pollinators.

name: Wool Carder Bee
funFact: Wool carder bees scrape plant hairs to line their nests, hence their name.
description: Wool carder bees are solitary bees that collect plant hairs to line their nest cells. Males aggressively defend patches of fuzzy plants where females forage for nesting material.

name: Cicada Killer Wasp
habitat: Sandy soils and sunny areas near trees
funFact: The cicada killer is the largest wasp in North America and can be over 2 inches long.
description: The cicada killer is a massive solitary wasp that hunts cicadas to provision its underground nest. Despite its intimidating size, it rarely stings humans unless provoked.

name: Red Velvet Ant
funFact: The velvet ant is actually a wingless wasp with one of the most painful stings in the insect world.
description: The red velvet ant is a wingless female wasp with a dense covering of bright red hairs. Despite its ant-like appearance, it is a parasitoid wasp whose sting is extremely painful.

name: Cuckoo Bumblebee
funFact: Cuckoo bumblebees infiltrate other bumblebee nests and lay their eggs for the host to raise.
description: Cuckoo bumblebees are social parasites that take over the nests of other bumblebee species. The female cuckoo bumblebee displaces the host queen and lays her own eggs for the workers to tend.

name: Asian Tiger Mosquito
habitat: Urban and suburban areas, standing water
funFact: Only female mosquitoes bite, needing blood protein to produce eggs.
description: The Asian tiger mosquito is an invasive species that can transmit dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses. It is identified by its distinctive black and white striped body and legs.

name: Common House Fly
habitat: Near human habitation and livestock worldwide
funFact: House flies taste with their feet and can detect food from miles away.
description: The common house fly is one of the most widespread insects, closely associated with humans. It has sponging mouthparts for liquid feeding and can transmit numerous diseases.

name: Common Fruit Fly
habitat: Near rotting fruit and fermented foods
funFact: Fruit flies are one of the most important model organisms in genetics research.
description: The common fruit fly is tiny but remarkably important in scientific research. They reproduce rapidly and share many genes with humans, making them invaluable for studying genetics and disease.

name: Crane Fly
funFact: Crane flies are often mistakenly called giant mosquitoes but do not bite or suck blood.
description: Crane flies are delicate, long-legged insects that resemble oversized mosquitoes. Adults are harmless and many do not feed at all, while their larvae, known as leatherjackets, live in soil.

name: Horse Fly
habitat: Near water, marshes, and livestock areas
funFact: Horse flies are among the fastest flying insects, reaching speeds up to 90 mph.
description: Horse flies are large, powerful fliers with razor-sharp mouthparts that slash skin to feed on blood. Only females bite, and their painful bites can transmit diseases to livestock and humans.

name: Human Bot Fly
funFact: Bot fly larvae develop under human skin, creating painful boils called myiasis.
description: The human bot fly is a parasitic insect whose larvae develop beneath the skin of mammals, including humans. Adults do not bite; instead, they hijack mosquitoes to deliver their eggs to hosts.

name: Common Hover Fly
funFact: Hover flies mimic bees and wasps for protection but are completely harmless.
description: Hover flies are beneficial pollinators that mimic the appearance of stinging insects for protection. Their larvae are important predators of aphids, making them valuable in pest control.

name: Black Fly
funFact: Black fly swarms can be so dense that they suffocate livestock by blocking their airways.
description: Black flies are tiny but relentless biting insects that breed in flowing water. In some regions they transmit river blindness and are considered one of the most important disease vectors.

name: Common Green Darner
funFact: Dragonflies can fly in all six directions and hover like a helicopter.
description: Dragonflies are ancient aerial predators with enormous compound eyes and two pairs of independently controlled wings. They are among the most efficient hunters in the insect world.

name: Blue-Tailed Damselfly
funFact: Damselflies fold their wings along their bodies when at rest, unlike dragonflies.
description: Damselflies are slender, delicate relatives of dragonflies that hold their wings together above their body when resting. They are important aquatic ecosystem indicators and voracious mosquito predators.

name: Blue Dasher Dragonfly
funFact: Blue dashers can fly backwards and hover in place like a helicopter.
description: The blue dasher is a small, common dragonfly with a blue-green body and distinctive wing pattern. It is an agile aerial predator that catches mosquitoes and other small insects on the wing.

name: Emperor Dragonfly
funFact: Emperor dragonflies can eat their own body weight in insects every day.
description: The emperor dragonfly is one of the largest and most powerful dragonflies in Europe. It patrols territories over water and feeds voraciously on mosquitoes, flies, and other flying insects.

name: Four-Spotted Chaser
funFact: Four-spotted chasers are among the first dragonflies to emerge in spring.
description: The four-spotted chaser is a robust dragonfly with distinctive dark spots on its wings. It is an aggressive territorial species that perches on vegetation to ambush passing prey.

name: Robber Fly
funFact: Robber flies can capture and eat insects as large as dragonflies and grasshoppers.
description: Robber flies are aerial predators that intercept prey in flight. They inject victims with saliva that paralyzes and digests their insides, then suck out the liquefied contents.

name: Marmalade Hoverfly
funFact: Marmalade hoverflies migrate thousands of miles across Europe each year.
description: The marmalade hoverfly is a bee-mimic hoverfly that is an important pollinator. Its larvae are voracious aphid predators, making it doubly valuable in gardens and agriculture.

name: Common Mosquito
habitat: Near standing water and human habitation
funFact: Mosquitoes are responsible for more human deaths than any other animal in history.
description: Mosquitoes are small, buzzing flies that transmit deadly diseases including malaria, dengue, and Zika. Only females bite to obtain blood for egg production, while males feed on nectar.

name: Biting Midge
funFact: Biting midges, or no-see-ums, are so small they can pass through standard window screens.
description: Biting midges are tiny flies that deliver disproportionately painful bites. They are among the smallest biting flies and can be major pests in coastal and tropical regions.

name: Deer Fly
funFact: Deer flies are attracted to dark colors and carbon dioxide, similar to mosquitoes.
description: Deer flies are fast-flying, aggressive biters with patterned wings. They transmit tularemia and can cause severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

name: Cattle Bot Fly
funFact: Cattle bot fly larvae attach to the tongues and throat of cattle, causing significant irritation.
description: The cattle bot fly is a parasitic fly whose larvae develop in the throats of cattle. Adults are bee-like in appearance and do not feed, living only long enough to reproduce.

name: Chinese Praying Mantis
funFact: Praying mantises can rotate their heads 180 degrees to scan for prey.
description: The Chinese praying mantis is a large, elongated predatory insect with triangular head and powerful raptorial front legs. It is a sit-and-wait ambush predator of other insects.

name: Orchid Mantis
funFact: The orchid mantis looks so much like a flower that pollinators land directly on it.
description: The orchid mantis is a stunning pink and white mantis that mimics orchid flowers to ambush pollinators. It is considered one of the most beautiful insects in the world.

name: Ghost Mantis
habitat: Tropical forests of Madagascar and Africa
funFact: The ghost mantis looks exactly like a dried, dead leaf, making it nearly invisible.
description: The ghost mantis is a master of camouflage with a body shaped and colored to resemble a dried leaf. It sways gently to mimic a leaf in the wind, hiding from both predators and prey.

name: Dead Leaf Mantis
funFact: The dead leaf mantis has irregular body edges that perfectly replicate a torn, decaying leaf.
description: The dead leaf mantis is a large, spectacular mantis with a flattened body resembling a dead leaf. It is an ambush predator that waits motionless for prey to come within striking distance.

name: Common Walking Stick
funFact: Walking sticks can regenerate lost limbs during molts and some species produce toxic defensive chemicals.
description: Walking sticks are elongated, camouflaged insects that resemble twigs or branches. They are nocturnal herbivores that rely on their extraordinary disguise to avoid detection by predators.

name: Giant Walking Stick
funFact: The giant walking stick holds the record for the longest insect in the world.
description: The giant walking stick, also known as Chan's megastick, is the longest insect species, with females reaching over 14 inches including legs. It is native to Borneo's tropical rainforests.

name: American Cockroach
habitat: Sewers, basements, and warm, humid areas
funFact: Cockroaches can survive for weeks without food and hold their breath for 40 minutes.
description: The American cockroach is the largest common cockroach found in human habitations. Despite its name, it originated in Africa and is now found worldwide in warm, moist environments.

name: German Cockroach
funFact: German cockroaches can produce up to 30,000 offspring in a single year from one female.
description: The German cockroach is the most troublesome indoor cockroach species worldwide. It reproduces rapidly, is resistant to many insecticides, and contaminates food and surfaces with pathogens.

name: Madagascar Hissing Cockroach
funFact: Madagascar hissing cockroaches produce a loud hiss by forcing air through specialized breathing holes.
description: The Madagascar hissing cockroach is one of the largest cockroach species, reaching 3 inches long. It is famous for the loud hissing sound it produces when disturbed, used for defense and communication.

name: Oriental Cockroach
habitat: Cool, damp areas like basements and drains
funFact: Oriental cockroaches are sometimes called water bugs because they prefer damp, dark environments.
description: The oriental cockroach is a large, dark species that prefers cool, damp environments. It is a scavenger that feeds on decaying organic matter and is associated with poor sanitation.

name: Eastern Subterranean Termite
habitat: Underground colonies beneath soil and wood
funFact: Subterranean termite colonies can contain millions of individuals working together.
description: Eastern subterranean termites are the most destructive termite species in North America. They live in underground colonies and build mud tubes to reach wood structures above ground.

name: Formosan Subterranean Termite
habitat: Subterranean colonies in warm, humid climates
funFact: Formosan termites build carton nests above ground and can consume a foot of 2x4 lumber in about five months.
description: The Formosan termite is one of the most destructive termite species, capable of consuming enormous amounts of wood. Unlike most termites, it can build above-ground nests, making it especially destructive.
region: East Asia (invasive in southern United States)

name: Dampwood Termite
habitat: Moist, decaying wood and damp soil
funFact: Dampwood termites are the largest North American termites and do not require soil contact.
description: Dampwood termites infest moist, decaying wood and are indicators of excessive moisture problems. They are larger than subterranean termites and do not build mud tubes.

name: Drywood Termite
habitat: Dry wood in structures and dead trees
funFact: Drywood termites kick out tiny fecal pellets called frass that accumulate below infested wood.
description: Drywood termites live entirely within the wood they consume and do not require soil contact. They are difficult to detect and treat because colonies can be scattered throughout a structure.
region: Southern United States and tropical regions

name: Periodical Cicada
habitat: Deciduous forests of eastern North America
funFact: Periodical cicadas emerge in synchronized broods of billions after 13 or 17 years underground.
description: Periodical cicadas are famous for their synchronized mass emergences every 13 or 17 years. They are the longest-lived insects and their emergences create deafening choruses heard for miles.

name: Dog-Day Cicada
habitat: Forests and suburban areas of North America
funFact: Dog-day cicadas get their name because they emerge during the dog days of summer.
description: Dog-day cicadas are annual cicadas that emerge each summer, unlike their periodical cousins. Their loud buzzing songs fill late summer afternoons in eastern North America.

name: Masked Devil Cicada
habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions of Australia
funFact: Some Australian cicada species have the loudest insect calls, exceeding 120 decibels.
description: The masked devil cicada is an Australian species known for its distinctive facial markings. Like other cicadas, it spends years underground before emerging for a brief, noisy adult life.

name: Brown Planthopper
habitat: Rice fields and grasslands of Asia
funFact: Brown planthoppers can jump 70 times their body length in a single leap.
description: The brown planthopper is a major pest of rice crops in Asia. It feeds on plant sap and transmits the devastating rice ragged stunt virus and rice grassy stunt virus.

name: Meadow Spittlebug
funFact: Spittlebug nymphs produce foamy saliva masses called cuckoo spit to protect themselves.
description: Spittlebugs get their name from the frothy foam masses their nymphs produce on plant stems. These nymphs, called froghoppers, are sap-sucking insects that can transmit plant diseases.

name: Green Peach Aphid
funFact: Aphids can produce up to 80 offspring per female without mating through parthenogenesis.
description: The green peach aphid is one of the most destructive agricultural pests worldwide. It reproduces rapidly through asexual reproduction and transmits over 100 plant viruses.

name: Common Bed Bug
habitat: Bedding, furniture, and cracks in walls
funFact: Bed bugs can survive for over a year without feeding and are resistant to many pesticides.
description: Bed bugs are parasitic insects that feed on human blood at night. They hide in mattress seams, furniture, and wall cracks, and their populations have surged worldwide due to pesticide resistance.

name: Triatomine Bug
habitat: Cracks in walls and thatched roofs of Latin America
funFact: Kissing bugs are called so because they often bite people on the face while they sleep.
description: Triatomine bugs, also known as kissing bugs, are vectors of Chagas disease. They feed on blood at night and transmit the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi through their feces.

name: Brown Marmorated Stink Bug
funFact: Stink bugs release a foul-smelling chemical from glands on their thorax when disturbed.
description: The brown marmorated stink bug is an invasive species from Asia that has become a major agricultural pest in North America. It damages fruit crops and invades homes in winter seeking shelter.
region: East Asia (invasive in North America and Europe)

name: Box Elder Bug
habitat: Near box elder trees and buildings
funFact: Box elder bugs aggregate in huge numbers on warm south-facing walls in autumn.
description: Box elder bugs are black insects with red markings that feed on box elder tree seeds. They become nuisances in fall when they cluster on buildings seeking warmth for winter.

name: Common Water Strider
funFact: Water striders can walk on water due to microscopic hairs on their legs that trap air.
description: Water striders are insects that glide across the surface of calm water using surface tension. Their hydrophobic leg hairs create air cushions that keep them afloat while they hunt prey.

name: Giant Water Bug
funFact: Giant water bugs are called toe-biters and can deliver an extremely painful bite.
description: Giant water bugs are large, flat-bodied aquatic predators that prey on fish, frogs, and snakes. Males carry eggs on their backs and are sometimes called electric-light bugs for their attraction to lights.

name: American Bird Grasshopper
funFact: Bird grasshoppers are strong fliers and can travel significant distances during migrations.
description: The American bird grasshopper is a large, strong-flying grasshopper that feeds on a wide variety of plants. It gets its name from its bird-like flight and large size.

name: Desert Locust
habitat: Arid and semi-arid regions of Africa and Asia
funFact: Desert locust swarms can cover 460 square miles and contain 40 to 80 billion insects.
description: The desert locust is the most destructive of all locust species. Under certain conditions it transforms from a solitary grasshopper into a gregarious swarming phase capable of devastating crops.
region: Africa, Middle East, and South Asia

name: Mormon Cricket
habitat: Rangelands and sagebrush steppe of western North America
funFact: Despite their name, Mormon crickets are actually shield-backed katydids, not true crickets.
description: The Mormon cricket is not a cricket but a large shield-backed katydid that forms migrating bands of billions. They were named after Mormon settlers whose crops they devastated in the 1840s.

name: Field Cricket
funFact: Male field crickets chirp by rubbing their wings together, and you can estimate temperature by counting chirps.
description: Field crickets are known for their distinctive chirping songs produced by males to attract mates. They are omnivorous scavengers that feed on plants, fungi, and other insects.

name: True Katydid
funFact: Katydid songs are ultrasonic, making them difficult for humans to hear without special equipment.
description: True katydids are named after their call, said to sound like Katy-did, Katy-didn't. They are leaf-mimicking insects that produce loud, clicking songs at ultrasonic frequencies.

name: European Mole Cricket
funFact: Mole crickets can swim and fly, making them highly mobile pests of turfgrass.
description: Mole crickets are burrowing insects with powerful, shovel-like forelegs adapted for digging through soil. They damage lawns and crops by feeding on roots and disrupting soil structure.

name: Snowy Tree Cricket
funFact: The snowy tree cricket is known as the thermometer cricket because chirp rate correlates with temperature.
description: The snowy tree cricket produces a pure, musical trill and is famous for its temperature-dependent chirping rate. Dolbear's Law uses its chirps to estimate ambient temperature.

name: Human Head Louse
funFact: Head lice have been companions of humans for at least 10,000 years.
description: Human head lice are parasitic insects that live on the scalp and feed on blood. They are wingless and highly adapted to life on humans, spreading through direct head-to-head contact.

name: Human Body Louse
funFact: Body lice have been used to track human migration patterns through DNA analysis.
description: Human body lice live in clothing and emerge to feed on blood. Unlike head lice, they can transmit serious diseases including typhus, trench fever, and relapsing fever.

name: Human Flea
habitat: Nests, burrows, and bedding of mammals
funFact: Fleas can jump up to 150 times their body length, equivalent to a human jumping over a skyscraper.
description: The human flea, Pulex irritans, is the original flea species associated with humans. It is a blood-feeding parasite that can transmit diseases and has been a companion of humans for millennia.

name: Cat Flea
habitat: Fur of cats, dogs, and other mammals
funFact: Cat fleas are the most common flea species on domestic pets worldwide.
description: The cat flea is the most common flea species affecting domestic cats and dogs. Despite its name, it infests many mammal species and can cause allergic dermatitis and transmit tapeworms.

name: Oriental Rat Flea
funFact: The oriental rat flea was the primary vector of bubonic plague during the Black Death.
description: The oriental rat flea is historically the most important disease vector among fleas, having transmitted bubonic plague during the Black Death. It feeds primarily on rats and other rodents.

name: Southern Black Widow Spider
funFact: The black widow's venom is 15 times stronger than a rattlesnake's, but less is injected.
description: The southern black widow is one of North America's most venomous spiders. Females are recognized by the red hourglass marking on their abdomen and sometimes eat the male after mating.

name: Brown Recluse Spider
funFact: Brown recluse venom can cause necrotic lesions that take months to heal.
description: The brown recluse spider has a violin-shaped marking on its cephalothorax and venom that can cause tissue death. It is reclusive and bites only when pressed against skin.

name: Common Wolf Spider
funFact: Wolf spider mothers carry their egg sacs and spiderlings on their backs.
description: Wolf spiders are agile, ground-hunting spiders that do not build webs. They have excellent vision and chase down their prey, and females are notable for carrying their young on their backs.

name: Bold Jumping Spider
habitat: Walls, fences, and vegetation near buildings
funFact: Jumping spiders have the best vision of any spider and can jump 50 times their body length.
description: Bold jumping spiders are charismatic, fuzzy spiders with large forward-facing eyes. They are active hunters that stalk prey and leap to capture it, displaying complex courtship dances.

name: Garden Orb Weaver Spider
funFact: Orb weavers rebuild their webs almost every night, consuming the old silk to recycle the proteins.
description: Garden orb weavers are among the most common web-building spiders. They create distinctive circular webs and are beneficial predators of flying insects in gardens and natural areas.

name: Peacock Spider
habitat: Coastal heathlands and shrublands of Australia
funFact: Male peacock spiders perform elaborate dance displays with colorful abdominal flaps to court females.
description: Peacock spiders are tiny jumping spiders famous for the males' spectacular iridescent abdominal flaps used in elaborate courtship dances. Females will eat males who fail to impress.

name: Mexican Red-Kneed Tarantula
habitat: Scrublands and desert regions of Mexico
funFact: Tarantulas urinate from their fangs, using digestive fluid rather than water.
description: The Mexican red-kneed tarantula is a large, docile spider popular in the pet trade. It has urticating hairs on its abdomen that it can flick at threats, causing skin irritation.

name: Brazilian Wandering Spider
habitat: Tropical forests of Central and South America
funFact: The Brazilian wandering spider has the most potent venom of any spider and is listed in Guinness World Records.
description: The Brazilian wandering spider is considered the world's most venomous spider. Unlike web-building spiders, it actively wanders the forest floor at night and can deliver a medically significant bite.

name: Emperor Scorpion
funFact: Emperor scorpions glow bright blue-green under ultraviolet light.
description: The emperor scorpion is one of the largest scorpion species and one of the most popular in the pet trade. Despite its intimidating size, its venom is relatively mild and it is generally docile.

name: Arizona Bark Scorpion
habitat: Desert regions and urban areas of the southwestern US
funFact: Arizona bark scorpions are the most venomous scorpion in North America and can climb walls and ceilings.
description: The Arizona bark scorpion is the most dangerous scorpion in North America. It is unique among scorpions in its ability to climb walls and ceilings, often entering homes through plumbing.
region: Southwestern United States and Northern Mexico

name: Deathstalker Scorpion
habitat: Deserts and scrublands of North Africa and Middle East
funFact: The deathstalker's venom contains compounds being researched for use in cancer treatment.
description: The deathstalker is one of the most venomous scorpions in the world. Its potent neurotoxic venom can be fatal to humans, but its venom compounds show promise in medical research.

name: Spotted Lanternfly
funFact: Spotted lanternflies can lay up to 50 eggs on almost any flat surface.
description: The spotted lanternfly is an invasive planthopper from Asia that feeds on over 70 plant species, threatening agriculture. Adults have distinctive spotted wings and bright red hind wings.
region: East Asia (invasive in eastern United States)

name: Wheel Bug
funFact: The wheel bug gets its name from the distinctive cogwheel-like crest on its thorax.
description: The wheel bug is a large, beneficial predatory insect with a distinctive semicircular crest on its thorax. It uses its proboscis to inject digestive enzymes into prey and is a natural pest controller.

name: Rose Slug Sawfly
funFact: Sawfly larvae look like caterpillars but have more than five pairs of prolegs.
description: Sawflies are wasp-like insects whose larvae feed on plant foliage, resembling caterpillars. The rose slug sawfly can skeletonize rose leaves, causing significant damage to gardens.

name: Antlion
habitat: Sandy soils in warm, dry areas
funFact: Antlion larvae dig conical pit traps in sand to catch ants and other small insects.
description: Antlions are insects whose larvae are famous for digging conical pitfall traps in sand. They wait at the bottom of the pit for prey to fall in, then inject digestive enzymes.

name: Green Lacewing
funFact: Lacewing larvae are called aphid lions and can each consume 200 aphids per week.
description: Green lacewings are delicate, golden-green insects with lace-like wings. Their larvae are voracious predators of aphids and other soft-bodied pests, making them valuable biological control agents.

name: Eastern Dobsonfly
funFact: Dobsonfly larvae, called hellgrammites, are indicators of good water quality.
description: The eastern dobsonfly is a large, impressive insect with enormous wings and males have extremely long mandibles. The aquatic larvae are important food for trout and indicators of stream health.

name: Mayfly
habitat: Near clean rivers, streams, and lakes
funFact: Adult mayflies have vestigial mouthparts and cannot eat, living only long enough to mate.
description: Mayflies are aquatic insects with extremely short adult lifespans dedicated solely to reproduction. Their larvae are important indicators of water quality and food for fish.

name: Common European Earwig
habitat: Gardens, compost piles, and under stones
funFact: Earwig mothers guard their eggs and clean them to prevent fungal growth.
description: The common European earwig is a nocturnal insect with distinctive pincer-like cerci on its abdomen. Despite myths, earwigs do not burrow into human ears, and mothers provide notable parental care.

name: Common Silverfish
habitat: Homes, libraries, and dark, humid areas
funFact: Silverfish are among the most primitive wingless insects, virtually unchanged for 400 million years.
description: Silverfish are small, wingless, silver-colored insects that damage paper, textiles, and food. They are nocturnal and thrive in warm, humid environments like bathrooms and basements.

name: Firebrat
habitat: Near furnaces, fireplaces, and hot attics
funFact: Firebrats prefer temperatures above 90 degrees Fahrenheit and can survive scorching conditions.
description: Firebrats are close relatives of silverfish that prefer much warmer environments. They are found near heat sources like furnaces and water heaters and feed on starchy materials.

name: Jumping Bristletail
habitat: Rocky shores, caves, and stone walls
funFact: Jumping bristletails are among the most ancient insects, with a fossil record dating back 400 million years.
description: Jumping bristletails are small, wingless insects that can jump by curling their abdomen. They are found in moist environments and feed on algae, lichens, and decaying plant matter.

name: Snakefly
funFact: Snakefly larvae can crawl backwards at high speed to escape threats.
description: Snakeflies are predatory insects with an elongated prothorax that gives them a snake-like appearance. Both adults and larvae are beneficial predators of pest insects on trees.

name: Bombus Bob
habitat: Meadows and grasslands of North America
funFact: Some cuckoo bumblebee species have been reclassified as entirely separate species from their hosts.
description: This cuckoo bumblebee species is a social parasite that takes over nests of other bumblebee species. The female enters a host nest, kills or displaces the queen, and uses the existing workers.

name: Musk Bee
habitat: Dry, sandy soils and open areas
funFact: Musk bees produce a distinctive lemony scent when disturbed.
description: The musk bee is a solitary ground-nesting bee known for its distinctive musky scent. It emerges in late summer and is an important pollinator of goldenrod and other fall wildflowers.

name: Alkali Bee
habitat: Alkaline soils near salt flats and playas
funFact: Alkali bees prefer salty, alkaline soil for nesting and can form massive aggregations.
description: The alkali bee is a solitary ground-nesting bee that prefers alkaline soils near salt flats. It is an excellent pollinator of alfalfa and has been managed commercially for this purpose.

name: Black Carpenter Ant
habitat: Moist, decaying wood and structural timbers
funFact: Carpenter ants do not eat wood but excavate it to create nesting galleries.
description: Black carpenter ants are large ants that excavate nests in moist, decaying wood. Unlike termites, they do not consume wood but can cause structural damage by hollowing out timbers.

name: Pharaoh Ant
funFact: Pharaoh ants can nest in extremely small spaces and are known to spread disease in hospitals.
description: Pharaoh ants are tiny, pale-colored invasive ants that are particularly problematic in hospitals and food facilities. They form huge colonies with multiple queens and bud frequently.

name: Odorous House Ant
habitat: Under objects on the ground and inside buildings
funFact: Odorous house ants smell like crushed coconut when squished.
description: Odorous house ants are common household ants that emit a distinctive coconut-like odor when crushed. They form large colonies and frequently nest inside walls and under floors.
